note: Salesforce JWT Auth Provider adds key-based (JWT bearer) auth via two @SalesforceAuthProvider plugins: jwt and jwt_govcloud. Each authorization is a salesforce_auth config entity with provider=jwt and provider_settings (login_url, consumer_key, username, encrypt_key referencing a Key entity). Creating/reading the auth config entity is local (no connection needed - only AUTHORIZING/token exchange needs the org), so all medium/hard cases are grounded in real salesforce_auth config entities created/read/modified locally and verified by pure reads. Namespaced sfj_* auth entities are removed on cleanup.

evals.prompt: What kind of Salesforce authentication does the Salesforce JWT Auth Provider module add, and what are its plugin ids?
evals.expected_output: It adds key-based JWT bearer (server-to-server) authentication - no interactive login. It provides the auth-provider plugins jwt and jwt_govcloud, which sign a JWT assertion with a private key stored via the Key module.

evals.prompt: When configuring a JWT Salesforce authorization, what settings do you provide (consumer key, login URL, key, user), and where is the private signing key stored?
evals.expected_output: A jwt salesforce_auth stores provider_settings: login_url (production https://login.salesforce.com or sandbox https://test.salesforce.com), consumer_key (connected app), username (to impersonate), and encrypt_key - the id of a Key module entity holding the private key that signs the JWT.

evals.prompt: For a JWT Salesforce authorization, what login_url do I use to connect to a Salesforce sandbox versus production?
evals.expected_output: Use https://test.salesforce.com for a sandbox and https://login.salesforce.com for production, set as the login_url in the jwt authorization's provider_settings.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a Salesforce authorization named sfj_known. Inspect its live configuration and state which auth provider it uses.
evals.expected_output: It uses the jwt provider: salesforce_auth sfj_known has provider = jwt (key-based JWT authentication).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a JWT Salesforce authorization named sfj_env. Inspect its live configuration and state its login URL - is it pointing at production or a sandbox?
evals.expected_output: It points at production: salesforce_auth sfj_env has provider_settings.login_url = https://login.salesforce.com.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, create a Salesforce authorization named sfj_task that uses key-based JWT authentication (the jwt provider). Apply the change to the live site (you do not need to complete the token exchange with Salesforce).
evals.expected_output: A salesforce_auth config entity sfj_task exists with provider = jwt (created via the Salesforce auth UI or the salesforce_auth storage).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a JWT Salesforce authorization sfj_ltask currently pointed at a sandbox. Repoint it to production by setting its login URL to https://login.salesforce.com. Apply the change to the live site.
